{{short description|Point associated with any triangle}}
[[File:Tarry point.svg|300px|right|thumb]]

In [[geometry]], the '''Tarry point''' {{mvar|T}} for a [[triangle]] {{math|△''ABC''}} is a [[point (geometry)|point]] of [[concurrent lines|concurrency]] of the [[line segment|lines]] through the [[vertex (geometry)|vertices]] of the triangle [[perpendicular]] to the corresponding sides of the  triangle's first [[Brocard triangle]] {{math|△''DEF''}}. The Tarry point lies on the other endpoint of the [[diameter]] of the [[circumcircle]] drawn through the [[Steiner point (triangle)|Steiner point]].<ref>{{mathworld|urlname=TarryPoint|title=Tarry Point}}</ref> The point is named for [[Gaston Tarry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Tarry.html|title=Gaston Tarry|date=August 2006}}</ref>
